## S160001: exemptions are not shrink-only

The submitted file has the expected fifteen entries, but the checker trusts every supplied address. It has no approved-address baseline or comparison enforcing monotonic removal. `owner` and reason (`why`) are TypeScript declarations, not runtime validation.

A contributor can remove previously covered req-31's delivering workstream link and add that existing, genuinely uncovered address to the exemptions JSON. Stale/unknown checks accept it because it is now uncovered and still exists; the finding is suppressed, even without owner/reason. No checker-code change is required. The repository test at `harness/scripts/coverage-check.test.ts:100-103` accepts any positive exemption count.

Bind exemptions to a trusted approved baseline and enforce removals, rejecting additions, substitutions and reintroductions. Validate unique addresses and nonempty owner/reason at runtime. Add targeted tests for those proposed-file changes. This is not a claim that malicious maintainers cannot alter checker code; the bypass needs only proposed data changes.

## S160002: missing inputs are reported as coverage success

`readDocs` converts every directory-listing error to an empty list; `rows` similarly discards missing/non-array sections. Removing or making the blueprint directory unavailable, or replacing its components section with a non-array, makes component obligations disappear. Existing PRD exemptions remain valid, allowing universal coverage success with no unavailable-input finding.

Fail explicitly for unavailable required inputs and malformed required sections. An absent legacy alias directory can remain compatible only through a deliberate rule, not a blanket error-to-empty conversion. The unavailable CI ddocs step does not provide a compensating validation guard.

**Other boundaries:** new unexempted gaps, stale/nonexistent exemptions and unfinished umbrella children do produce findings. Missing exemption files and invalid exemption JSON propagate failure. Those controls do not establish shrink-only or fail-closed coverage inputs.

No prohibited publication disclosure found in the PR-owned delta. The atomic rename/schema commit and deliberate reader aliases retain the intended path transition. PM v4 preserves standing-packet quoting, authority and privacy/credential prohibitions; all 29 version pins and previous shipped bytes remain intact. Moved skill safety rules are not weakened.

**Proof:** source review against phase-1 baseline `59120b3`; exact-head CI [42393669106](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42393669106) passed all four jobs, and Node 22/24 each executed five coverage-check tests. Passing tests do not cover the missing policy boundary. F104/C20 ddocs remains UNAVAILABLE. AC7 is dry-run evidence only, with actual governance edits deferred until merge. No local builds/tests, dd installs, role edits, credential reads, live probes or product edits.
